messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> page fired for service=runtime-inference-prod env=prod
incident-bot: summary: p99 latency spike detected (threshold=1200ms) — current p95=420ms p99=1520ms across us-west and eu-west
incident-bot: matchers: metric=latency.p99 > 1200ms, alert_window=5m, severity=page
incident-bot: link: https://internal.metrics/graphs/runtime-inference-prod?view=p99 :rotating_light:
Maria: Acked on call. I’m looking. Any customer reports?
Jon: seeing a handful of 504s in logs for streaming endpoints, probably tail tokenization/backpressure. Checking KV cache hitrate and autoscaler events.
Carol: Noted elevated GC churn on sidecars earlier but nothing matching that magnitude. Can we reroute non-critical traffic to dedicated-pool-2 to relieve public fleet?
Maria: Initiating quick reroute to dedicated-pool-2 for routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat.low-prio. Will post commands.
Maria: ```
# quick reroute
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/route/rebind -d '{"from":"public-pool","to":"dedicated-pool-2","routes":["/v1/generate","/v1/chat.low-prio"]}'
# scale dedicated pool just in case
./infractl scale-pool --name dedicated-pool-2 --replicas 6
```
Jon: Good. I see autoscaler in us-west hit max and rejected scale requests ~2m ago. There are hot keys in KV cache from a small customer causing tail amplification. Dumping top keys.
Jon: ```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=kvcache --tail 200 | grep "hotkey" | head -n 20
# top key: customer:alpha:session:token -> ~18% of requests
```
Carol: If hotkey is from a single customer, we can shard or throttle them at the ingress for now. Recommend soft-throttle 20r/s with a header 429 to avoid full cascade.
Maria: Applying ingress throttling rule for alpha tenant now.
Maria: ```
# ingress throttle
./gatewayctl set-rate-limit --tenant alpha --route "/v1/*" --rate 20
```
pagerduty: Escalation: page not acknowledged by level2 within 5m, escalating to SRE rotation.
Dave: I’m coming in — brief me.
Maria: Summary: p99 spike 1520ms, p95 420ms, hotkey from tenant alpha causing KV cache hotspot and autoscaler saturation. We routed low-priority traffic to dedicated-pool-2 and applied ingress throttle for alpha. Scaling dedicated pool to +3 replicas.
Dave: Thanks. I’ll watch for degradation and coordinate customer comms if errors persist. Any change in error rate?
Jon: Error 504s peaked at ~1.3% of requests. After reroute + throttle, 504s falling to 0.4% and p99 trending down to ~600ms in us-west. eu-west still at ~900ms.
Maria: rolling a lighter-weight tokenizer build to edge sidecars in eu-west to mitigate cold start tokenization overhead — small canary now.
Carol: Can we enable fallback model (quantized variant) for streaming endpoints as temporary measure? That will lower accuracy but reduce compute pressure.
Maria: Enabling fallback: executed for 10% traffic now.
incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty -> incident acknowledged by Maria at 1747773020.
pagerduty: Update: level2 escalated and Dave acknowledged at 1747773065.
Jon: After routing + throttle + fallback, p99 global = 460ms, p95 = 210ms. eu-west p99 = 520ms. Error rate steady at 0.15%.
Dave: Looks stable. Keep watching for 15m. We should prepare a short customer-facing note if eu-west lingers.
Maria: Will draft a bulletin and handoff to next on-call in 30m if stable. Logging mitigation steps for postmortem.
Carol: Add a follow-up to evaluate hotkey detection and automated micro-throttling to avoid autoscaler saturation next time.
Maria: Thanks all — big :thumbsup: to the quick reroute and throttle. I’ll update the incident board and tag for postmortem.
Dave: I’ll take the handoff at 1747773180 if still green and start timeline.
Maria: final check — p99 now ~420ms across regions, closing page for now, will keep monitor for 1 hour.
incident-bot: Page closed by Maria at 1747773180.
